mcq.q: Which of these is a sign of life in plants?
mcq.explanation: Plants grow, reproduce, remove waste, respond and die. They do not walk or make noise.

mcq.q: Which of these is NOT alive?
mcq.explanation: A plastic flower is made by people and does not grow, respond or reproduce.

mcq.q: How do most flowering plants make new plants?
mcq.explanation: Most flowering plants reproduce by making seeds inside fruits.

mcq.q: A sweet potato vine cutting grows roots and becomes a new plant. Which sign of life is shown?
mcq.explanation: Making a new plant from part of an old plant is reproduction.

mcq.q: The touch-me-not plant folds its leaves when touched. This shows that plants can
mcq.explanation: Folding when touched is a response to a change in the surroundings.

mcq.q: A plant on a windowsill grows towards the window. What is it responding to?
mcq.explanation: Plants bend and grow towards light coming from one side.

mcq.q: Which sign of life do ALL living things eventually show?
mcq.explanation: Every living thing dies one day, but not all fly, flower or make seeds.

mcq.q: What does removing waste mean for a plant?
options: Getting rid of things its body does not need
mcq.explanation: Living things must remove waste made in their bodies.

mcq.q: Which part of the plant holds it firmly in the soil?
mcq.explanation: Roots anchor the plant in the ground.

mcq.q: Which part of the plant takes in water from the soil?
mcq.explanation: Roots take in water and mineral salts.

mcq.q: What is the main job of leaves?
options: Holding the plant in the soil
Taking in water from the soil
mcq.explanation: Leaves use sunlight, water and air to make food.

mcq.q: What does the stem do?
options: Holds up the plant and carries water and food
mcq.explanation: The stem supports the plant and carries water and food.

mcq.q: Which part of a plant makes fruits and seeds?
mcq.explanation: Flowers make fruits that contain seeds.

mcq.q: Which of these is a root that we eat?
mcq.explanation: A carrot is a storage root. Cabbage is leaves, banana is a fruit and maize grain is a seed.

mcq.q: Which of these is a stem that stores food and is eaten or used for sugar?
mcq.explanation: Sugarcane stems store sugar.

mcq.q: Which part of the plant is usually flat, green and spread out to catch light?
mcq.explanation: The flat, green shape of a leaf helps it catch light.

mcq.q: What comes out of a bean seed first when it starts to grow?
mcq.explanation: The root comes out first and grows down into the soil.

mcq.q: Which of these do plants need to stay alive?
mcq.explanation: Plants need water, air, light and nutrients from the soil.

mcq.q: A plant with no water for many days will
mcq.explanation: Water is needed for life, so a plant without it wilts and may die.

mcq.q: Maize lives for one season and then dies. A baobab lives for many years. What does this show?
options: Plants live for different lengths of time
mcq.explanation: All plants die, but some live for one season and others for many years.

mcq.q: Which is the best way of studying how a seedling grows?
options: Measure its height every two days
mcq.explanation: Measuring height regularly shows growth over time.

mcq.q: A student puts a plant in a box with a small hole on one side. After a week, the plant bends toward the hole. This shows that plants
mcq.explanation: The plant responds to the light entering through the hole.

mcq.q: Which of these shows a plant reproducing?
options: A bean plant making pods with seeds
mcq.explanation: Making seeds is reproduction. Growing taller is growth.

mcq.q: What are the two main types of things carried by the stem?
mcq.explanation: The stem carries water and mineral salts up and food made in leaves to other parts.

mcq.q: What is the word for the tiny parts in a leaf where air goes in and out?
mcq.explanation: Air moves in and out of leaves through tiny holes.

mcq.q: Why should you not pull leaves off a young plant for fun?
options: The plant needs its leaves to make food
The leaves make the roots sweet
The plant has too many leaves
mcq.explanation: Leaves are the food factories of the plant.

mcq.q: Which of these is a good way to care for plants at school?
options: Water them when the soil is dry
mcq.explanation: Watering when dry helps plants live and grow.

mcq.q: Which of these is a way that people benefit from plants?
options: They give food, shade and wood
mcq.explanation: Plants give us food, shade, medicine, wood and clean air.

mcq.q: Which part of a bean plant grows in the soil?
mcq.explanation: Roots grow underground.

mcq.q: Why do farmers remove weeds from a crop field?
options: So crops get enough water, light and space
mcq.explanation: Weeds compete with crops for water, light and room.

mcq.q: Which of these plant parts is usually colourful?
mcq.explanation: Flowers are often brightly coloured.

mcq.q: A student says a tree is not alive because it does not move from place to place. What is wrong with this idea?
options: Plants show life by growing and responding
mcq.explanation: Plants show many signs of life even though they do not walk.

mcq.q: In a seedling, what is the correct order of growth?
mcq.explanation: The seed starts, a root comes out, then a shoot with leaves.

mcq.q: What happens to a dead plant?
options: It rots and returns nutrients to the soil
mcq.explanation: Dead plants decay and give nutrients back to the soil.

mcq.q: Which sign of life is shown when a yellow leaf falls from a tree?
mcq.explanation: Old leaves may carry waste away when they fall.

mcq.q: Which of these is a plant that has a thick main root with thin side roots?
mcq.explanation: A bean plant has a main root with side roots. Maize and grass have many thin roots.

mcq.q: What do roots of cassava and sweet potato do besides taking in water?
mcq.explanation: These roots store food for the plant.

mcq.q: Which of these is a safety rule when handling plants?
options: Ask an adult before touching a plant you do not know
mcq.explanation: Some plants can hurt or poison people, so ask first.

mcq.q: What can you use to draw and label a plant if you have a computer at school?
mcq.explanation: A drawing app can be used to draw and label plant parts.

mcq.q: Which of these gives the young plant its first food before its leaves open?
mcq.explanation: The seed contains stored food that feeds the young plant at first.

mcq.q: Which of these is NOT a job of the roots?
options: Holding the plant in the soil
mcq.explanation: Fruits are made from flowers, not by roots.

mcq.q: In which part do you find the seeds of a mango?
mcq.explanation: Seeds are found inside fruits.

mcq.q: Which of these plants lives for many years?
options: Sukuma wiki grown for one season
mcq.explanation: Mango trees live for many years, while beans and maize live for one season.

mcq.q: Which of these is a sign of life in animals?
mcq.explanation: Animals feed, grow, breathe, reproduce, remove waste, move, respond and die.

mcq.q: Which of these is NOT an animal?
mcq.explanation: A toy is not alive. It does not feed, grow or reproduce.

mcq.q: Why do animals need to feed?
options: To get energy and to grow
mcq.explanation: Food gives animals energy and materials for growth.

mcq.q: Which of these do animals breathe in from the air?
mcq.explanation: Animals need oxygen from the air or water.

mcq.q: What do fish use to take oxygen from water?
mcq.explanation: Fish breathe using gills.

mcq.q: A caterpillar changes into a butterfly. Which sign of life does this best show?
mcq.explanation: A caterpillar grows and changes form to become a butterfly.

mcq.q: Which of these animals gives birth to live young?
mcq.explanation: Goats are mammals and give birth to live young. Hens, frogs and flies lay eggs.

mcq.q: Which of these animals lays eggs?
mcq.explanation: A hen lays eggs. The others give birth to live young.

mcq.q: What is the waste passed out by animals called?
mcq.explanation: Animals remove waste such as urine and faeces.

mcq.q: What does a snail do when you touch it?
options: Pulls its body into its shell
mcq.explanation: This is a response to touch.

mcq.q: What is a vertebrate?
options: An animal that lives in water only
mcq.explanation: Vertebrates have a backbone.

mcq.q: What is an invertebrate?
mcq.explanation: Invertebrates have no backbone.

mcq.q: Which of these is a vertebrate?
mcq.explanation: A hen is a bird and has a backbone.

mcq.q: Which of these is an invertebrate?
mcq.explanation: An earthworm has a soft body and no backbone.

mcq.q: Which group of vertebrates has feathers?
mcq.explanation: Only birds have feathers.

mcq.q: Which group of vertebrates feeds its young on milk?
mcq.explanation: Mammals feed their babies with milk.

mcq.q: Which group of animals has dry, scaly skin and includes snakes and crocodiles?
mcq.explanation: Reptiles have dry, scaly skin.

mcq.q: Frogs have smooth, wet skin and spend part of their life in water. They are
mcq.explanation: These features describe amphibians.

mcq.q: How many legs does an insect have?
mcq.explanation: All adult insects have six legs.

mcq.q: How many legs does a spider have?
mcq.explanation: Spiders have eight legs.

mcq.q: Why is a spider NOT an insect?
options: It has eight legs, not six
mcq.explanation: Insects have six legs and spiders have eight.

mcq.q: A bat flies but has fur and feeds its babies milk. What is it?
mcq.explanation: The fur and milk feeding make it a mammal.

mcq.q: Which of these is an insect?
mcq.explanation: A butterfly has six legs and three body parts.

mcq.q: Which of these animals has a soft body covered by a hard shell?
mcq.explanation: A snail has a soft body with a shell on its back.

mcq.q: Which of these is a mammal?
mcq.explanation: A cow has hair and feeds its calf on milk.

mcq.q: Which animal group breathes using gills?
mcq.explanation: Fish take oxygen from water with gills.

mcq.q: Which of these is a difference between plants and animals?
options: Animals move from place to place and take in ready-made food
Plants die but animals do not
Plants breathe and animals do not
mcq.explanation: Most animals move about and eat food, while plants make their own food.

mcq.q: A pupil finds a small animal under a stone. It has a long soft body, no legs and no shell. It is probably
mcq.explanation: An earthworm is a soft, legless invertebrate.

mcq.q: Which of these is a safe thing to do on a science walk?
options: Wash your hands after touching soil or animals
mcq.explanation: Handling animals safely and washing hands avoids injury and germs.

mcq.q: What should you do with a small animal after you observe it?
options: Take it home in your pocket
Return it to where you found it
mcq.explanation: Animals should be returned to their home.

mcq.q: Which of these is a good way to care for a farm animal?
mcq.explanation: Farm animals need water, food, shelter and care.

mcq.q: Which of these animals is a reptile?
mcq.explanation: A lizard has dry scaly skin.

mcq.q: Ostrich and flamingo belong to which group?
mcq.explanation: Both have feathers and lay eggs.

mcq.q: Which of these animals is an amphibian?
mcq.explanation: Toads have moist skin and start life in water.

mcq.q: Which of these is a crab?
options: An invertebrate with a hard outer shell
mcq.explanation: A crab has no backbone and has a hard shell outside.

mcq.q: What do vertebrates have inside their bodies that invertebrates do not?
mcq.explanation: A backbone is the feature that defines vertebrates.

mcq.q: A tadpole grows into a frog. What does this show?
mcq.explanation: Young animals grow and may change shape as they become adults.

mcq.q: Why is it important to protect wild animals and their homes?
options: They are part of nature and bring visitors to Kenya
They are dangerous to all people
mcq.explanation: Wild animals are part of our environment and bring income through tourism.

mcq.q: Which of these can you use to find out the differences between vertebrates and invertebrates?
mcq.explanation: We can search print and digital media for information.

mcq.q: A goat lifts its head when it hears a noise. Which sign of life is this?
mcq.explanation: The goat responds to a change in its surroundings, a sound.

mcq.q: Which of these is the best question to ask first when you sort an animal into vertebrate or invertebrate?
mcq.explanation: The backbone decides the group.

mcq.q: Which of these animals has an outside skeleton or hard covering and no backbone?
mcq.explanation: A crab has a hard outer shell and no backbone.

mcq.q: Which of these is a mammal that lives in water?
mcq.explanation: A whale breathes air and feeds milk to its calf, so it is a mammal even though it lives in water.

mcq.q: How do young mammals get their first food?
mcq.explanation: Mammals feed their babies with milk.

mcq.q: Which of these statements is true?
mcq.explanation: Fish are vertebrates. Small animals may be spiders, worms or others.

mcq.q: What is digestion?
options: Storing food in the stomach for years
Breaking down food into tiny parts the body can use
mcq.explanation: Digestion breaks food into tiny parts that can pass into the blood.

mcq.q: Where does the digestive tube begin?
mcq.explanation: Food enters the body through the mouth.

mcq.q: Where does the digestive tube end?
mcq.explanation: Waste leaves the body through the anus.

mcq.q: What is the correct order of parts food passes through?
mcq.explanation: Food goes from the mouth down the gullet to the stomach and then the small intestine.

mcq.q: What do teeth do in digestion?
options: Cut and grind food into small pieces
mcq.explanation: Chewing makes food smaller.

mcq.q: What is saliva?
options: A liquid in the mouth that wets food
mcq.explanation: Saliva wets food and starts to digest starchy foods.

mcq.q: Another name for the gullet is
mcq.explanation: The gullet is also called the oesophagus.

mcq.q: What does the gullet do?
options: Pushes swallowed food to the stomach
mcq.explanation: The gullet squeezes food down.

mcq.q: What does the stomach do to food?
options: Churns it and mixes it with juices
mcq.explanation: The stomach churns food into a thick soup with digestive juices.

mcq.q: Where does digestion finish and digested food pass into the blood?
mcq.explanation: The small intestine completes digestion and absorbs food into the blood.

mcq.q: What is absorption?
options: Digested food passing into the blood
mcq.explanation: Absorption means digested food parts pass into the blood.

mcq.q: Which part takes back most of the water from the leftover food?
mcq.explanation: The large intestine takes back water.

short.q: List four signs of life in plants.
short.answer: Any four of: grow, reproduce, remove waste, respond to changes, die.
short.working: 1 mark for two correct signs and 2 marks for four correct signs.

short.q: State two functions of roots.
short.answer: They hold the plant in the soil and take in water and mineral salts. Some store food.
short.working: 1 mark for each correct function.

short.q: Name the part of a plant that makes food and the part that makes seeds.
short.answer: Leaves make food and flowers (fruits) make seeds.
short.working: 1 mark for each correct part.

short.q: Explain why plants are called living things.
short.answer: They show signs of life. They grow, reproduce, remove waste, respond to changes and die.
short.working: 1 mark for saying they show signs of life and 2 marks for correct signs given.

short.q: Describe how a bean seed grows into a young plant.
short.answer: The seed takes in water and a root comes out first and goes down. Then a shoot grows up and opens into leaves.
short.working: 1 mark for water and seed, 1 mark for root first, 1 mark for shoot and leaves.

short.q: Give three examples of how plants respond to changes around them.
short.answer: Growing towards light, roots growing down, touch-me-not folding leaves, flowers opening in the day.
short.working: 1 mark for each correct example.

short.q: State three things that plants give to people.
short.answer: Food, shade, wood, medicine, clean air (any three).
short.working: 1 mark for each.

short.q: Why is it wrong to say that a tree is not alive because it cannot walk?
short.answer: Plants show life in other ways. They grow, reproduce, respond, remove waste and die. Only some animals walk.
short.working: 1 mark for stating plants show signs of life, 1 mark for naming signs, 1 mark for saying walking is not a sign needed for all living things.

short.q: Draw and label a plant showing roots, stem, leaves and flower.
short.answer: A drawing with four correctly labelled parts: roots below the ground, stem upright, leaves on the stem and a flower at the top.
short.working: 1 mark for each correctly drawn and labelled part.

short.q: Describe the function of each of these parts of a plant: roots, stem, leaves, flowers.
short.answer: Roots hold the plant and take in water. The stem supports the plant and carries water and food. Leaves make food. Flowers make fruits and seeds.
short.working: 1 mark for each correct function.

short.q: Explain what would happen to a young bean plant if all its leaves were removed and why.
short.answer: The plant would become weak and stop growing. Leaves make food for the plant. Roots can take in water but without leaves the plant cannot make enough food.
short.working: 1 mark for weak or stops growing, 1 mark for leaves make food, 1 mark for no food made, 1 mark for roots alone are not enough.

short.q: A pupil grows two bean seedlings. One is put in a cupboard and the other in the sunlight. Both are watered. After a week the two look different. Describe what she might see and give a reason.
short.answer: The plant in the cupboard looks weak and pale and the one in the light is green and healthy. Plants need light to make food.
short.working: 1 mark each for describing each plant and 2 marks for the reason.

short.q: Explain how a pupil can show that plants respond to light.
short.answer: Put a plant in a box with a hole on one side. After some days the plant bends towards the hole showing it responds to light.
short.working: 1 mark for the set up, 1 mark for the hole giving light from one side, 1 mark for the plant bending, 1 mark for conclusion.

short.q: Name two roots, two stems and two leaves that people eat.
short.answer: Roots: carrot, cassava, sweet potato. Stems: sugarcane. Leaves: cabbage, sukuma wiki, spinach (any two of each, with correct grouping).
short.working: 1 mark for each correct pair and 1 mark for correct grouping overall.

short.q: Describe how you can care for plants at school and at home. Give five ways.
short.answer: Water when dry, weed, do not trample, plant trees, do not pick flowers, put waste in bins, protect from animals (any five).
short.working: 1 mark for each way up to 5.

short.q: Describe an activity to observe the growth of a bean seed. Include what you need, what you do and what you record.
short.answer: You need a tin or container, soil, a bean seed and water. Plant the seed, water a little each day, measure the shoot with a ruler every two days and record heights in a table. Observe roots and leaves.
short.working: 1 mark for materials, 1 mark for planting, 1 mark for watering, 1 mark for measuring, 1 mark for recording.

short.q: A pupil pulls up a small bean plant from the garden. Describe what she will see and give the job of each part she sees.
short.answer: She will see roots that hold the plant and take in water, a stem that holds it up and carries food and water, leaves that make food, and maybe flowers or pods that make seeds.
short.working: 1 mark for naming each of four parts and 1 mark for correct function overall.

short.q: State any four signs of life in animals.
short.answer: Feeding, growing, breathing, reproducing, removing waste, moving, responding to changes, dying (any four).
short.working: 1 mark for two correct signs and 2 marks for four.

short.q: What is the difference between a vertebrate and an invertebrate?
short.answer: A vertebrate has a backbone and an invertebrate has no backbone.
short.working: 1 mark for each part.

short.q: Name two invertebrates that are found near your school.
short.answer: Any two correct examples such as ant, earthworm, snail, butterfly, spider.
short.working: 1 mark for each correct invertebrate.

short.q: Give two ways in which animals are different from plants.
short.answer: Animals can move from place to place. Animals feed on ready-made food while plants make their own.
short.working: 1 mark for each correct difference.

short.q: List the five groups of vertebrates and give one example of each.
short.answer: Mammals (goat), birds (hen), reptiles (snake), amphibians (frog), fish (tilapia).
short.working: 1 mark for correct five groups, 1 mark for four examples, 1 mark for correct matching.

short.q: Explain why a spider is not an insect.
short.answer: Insects have six legs and three body parts. A spider has eight legs, so it is not an insect. It is an invertebrate.
short.working: 1 mark for six legs, 1 mark for eight legs, 1 mark for conclusion.

short.q: Describe how a pupil can tell that an earthworm is an animal.
short.answer: It feeds on soil, grows, breathes, moves, responds to touch, reproduces and removes waste. It shows the signs of life.
short.working: 1 mark for each correct sign, up to 3.

short.q: Give three ways of caring for animals.
short.answer: Give food and clean water, provide shelter, keep their homes clean, treat sick animals, do not beat them.
short.working: 1 mark each.

short.q: A bat has wings. Explain why it is not a bird.
short.answer: A bat has fur and feeds its young on milk. Birds have feathers and lay eggs. So a bat is a mammal.
short.working: 1 mark for fur, 1 mark for milk, 1 mark for mammal.

short.q: Write three safety rules when observing animals in the school compound.
short.answer: Do not pick up animals you do not know, do not harm animals, wash hands after touching soil or animals, return animals to where they were found.
short.working: 1 mark for each rule.

short.q: Describe the differences between mammals and birds.
short.answer: Mammals have hair or fur and feed their young on milk and most give birth to live young. Birds have feathers and wings and lay eggs.
short.working: 1 mark for each of four differences.

short.q: Give two examples each of vertebrates and invertebrates, and state one feature of each group.
short.answer: Vertebrates: goat and tilapia, have a backbone. Invertebrates: ant and snail, have no backbone.
short.working: 1 mark for two vertebrates, 1 mark for feature, 1 mark for two invertebrates, 1 mark for feature.

short.q: Describe how animals respond to changes around them. Give four examples.
short.answer: A goat lifts its head at noise, a snail pulls into its shell when touched, birds fly away from danger, animals seek shade in hot weather.
short.working: 1 mark for the meaning and 1 mark for each of three examples.

short.q: Describe what you would put in a portfolio about vertebrates and invertebrates.
short.answer: A drawing of each animal, its name, whether it is a vertebrate or invertebrate, one sign of life seen, put together in a folder.
short.working: 1 mark for each of four items.

short.q: Explain how animals show the signs of life: feeding, growing, and reproducing. Give an example of each.
short.answer: Feeding: a goat eats grass. Growing: a chick becomes a hen. Reproducing: a hen lays eggs, or a cow gives birth.
short.working: 1 mark for each sign with example, plus 1 mark for explaining growth as getting bigger.

short.q: Explain how a frog is similar to and different from a fish.
short.answer: Both are vertebrates and have a backbone. A frog has moist skin and lives on land and in water, and a fish lives in water and has gills and fins.
short.working: 2 marks for similarity and 2 marks for differences.

short.q: Draw a table with two columns headed vertebrates and invertebrates. Place these animals correctly: goat, butterfly, snake, snail, hen, spider.
short.answer: Vertebrates: goat, snake, hen. Invertebrates: butterfly, snail, spider.
short.working: 1 mark for the table and 4 marks for placing the six animals (award 1 mark for two correct).

short.q: Describe the characteristics that show that animals are living things. Use examples.
short.answer: Animals feed, grow, breathe, reproduce, remove waste, move, respond and die. Give examples such as a goat eating grass and a hen laying eggs.
short.working: 1 mark for each sign to a maximum of 5.

short.q: Explain why we should care for animals and describe how it can be done at home and at school.
short.answer: Animals give us milk, meat, eggs and honey and help us in work. They are part of nature. We give them food, water, shelter and medical care and we do not hurt them. At school we keep the compound safe for birds.
short.working: 2 marks for reasons and 3 marks for ways.

short.q: Name the parts of the digestive system in the order food passes through them.
short.answer: Mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine, large intestine, rectum, anus.
short.working: Award 2 marks for the correct order. 1 mark if at most two parts are out of order.

short.q: State two jobs of the mouth in digestion.
short.answer: Teeth cut and grind food. The tongue moves food and saliva wets it and starts digesting starch.
short.working: 1 mark for each correct job.

short.q: Give two symptoms of an unhealthy digestive system.
short.answer: Stomach ache, bloating, diarrhoea, vomiting, constipation, worms (any two).
short.working: 1 mark each.

short.q: What happens in the large intestine?
short.answer: Water is taken back from the leftover food and the rest becomes faeces.
short.working: 1 mark for water and 1 mark for faeces.

short.q: Why is chewing food well important?
short.answer: It breaks food into small pieces and makes digestion easier.
short.working: 1 mark for small pieces and 1 mark for easier digestion.

short.q: Describe what happens to food in the stomach.
short.answer: The stomach churns the food and mixes it with strong juices. The juices kill many germs and break down the food into a thick soup.
short.working: 1 mark for churns, 1 mark for juices and 1 mark for germs or thick soup.

short.q: State three ways of keeping teeth healthy.
short.answer: Brush at least twice a day, limit sweets and sugary drinks, visit a dentist, use clean toothbrush or chewing stick.
short.working: 1 mark each.

short.q: Explain why we should wash our hands before eating and after using the toilet.
short.answer: Hands may carry germs and worm eggs. Washing removes them and stops them entering the mouth and causing disease.
short.working: 1 mark for germs on hands, 1 mark for washing removes them, 1 mark for preventing illness.

short.q: Explain how fibre helps the digestive system.
short.answer: Fibre in fruits, vegetables and whole grains helps food and waste move through the intestines and helps prevent constipation.
short.working: 1 mark for naming fibre foods, 1 mark for movement, 1 mark for constipation.

short.q: Write the function of the rectum and anus.
short.answer: The rectum stores faeces for a short time and the anus is the opening through which faeces leave the body.
short.working: 1 mark for rectum, 1 mark for anus, 1 mark for describing waste leaving.

short.q: State three things a child should do when he has diarrhoea.
short.answer: Tell an adult, drink clean water or ORS, and see a health worker. Keep clean.
short.working: 1 mark for each correct action.

short.q: Describe the journey of a mouthful of food from the mouth to the anus.
short.answer: Chewed in the mouth, swallowed, pushed down the gullet, churned in the stomach, digested and absorbed in the small intestine, water taken back in the large intestine, faeces stored in the rectum and passed out of the anus.
short.working: 1 mark for every two correct steps up to 4.

short.q: Explain why deworming is important and state two other ways of preventing worms.
short.answer: Worms live in the intestines and take food and make us weak. Deworming kills them. Wear shoes, wash hands, keep nails short.
short.working: 2 marks for reasons and 1 mark each for other ways.

short.q: Describe what happens in the small intestine and why it is important.
short.answer: Digestion is finished there. Digested food passes through the wall into the blood. The blood carries it to all parts of the body for energy, growth and repair.
short.working: 1 mark for each point up to 4.

short.q: Explain the difference between diarrhoea and constipation.
short.answer: Diarrhoea is passing loose watery faeces many times and causes loss of water. Constipation is passing hard dry faeces with difficulty.
short.working: 2 marks for each condition.

short.q: Give four healthy eating habits that keep the digestive system healthy.
short.answer: Eat a balanced diet, eat fruits and vegetables, drink clean water, chew slowly, wash fruits, avoid rotten food, cover food.
short.working: 1 mark for each habit up to 4.

short.q: Draw a simple diagram of the digestive system and label mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine, large intestine and anus.
short.answer: A neat tube drawn from mouth to anus with each part labelled in the correct order.
short.working: 1 mark for the drawing and 1 mark for each of four correct labels.

short.q: Make a plan for keeping your digestive system healthy for one week.
short.answer: A plan including brushing teeth twice a day, eating fruits and vegetables, drinking clean water, washing hands, chewing well, deworming as advised and limiting sweets.
short.working: 1 mark for each sensible action up to 5.

short.q: Describe the function of each part of the digestive system: mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine and large intestine.
short.answer: Mouth: chews and adds saliva. Gullet: pushes food down. Stomach: churns with juices. Small intestine: finishes digestion and absorbs food. Large intestine: takes back water.
short.working: 1 mark for each part.

short.q: Explain the dangers of diarrhoea and what should be done to help someone who has it.
short.answer: The body loses water quickly and the person becomes weak, especially young children. They should drink clean water and ORS, rest, see a health worker and keep clean.
short.working: 2 marks for dangers, 3 marks for actions.

short.q: Define matter and give two examples.
short.answer: Matter is anything that has mass and takes up space. Examples: water, stone, air.
short.working: 1 mark for the meaning and 1 mark for two examples.

short.q: Name the three states of matter and give one example of each.
short.answer: Solid (stone), liquid (water), gas (air).
short.working: Award 1 mark for the three states and 1 mark for correct examples.

short.q: State the difference between mass and volume.
short.answer: Mass is the amount of matter in an object and volume is the space it takes up.
short.working: 1 mark for each correct meaning.

short.q: Convert 3 litres into millilitres.
short.working: 1 mark for 3 x 1000 and 1 mark for the answer.

short.q: Convert 4 kg into grams.
short.working: 1 mark for 4 x 1000 and 1 mark for the answer with units.

short.q: Give two reasons why solids are useful in daily life.
short.answer: They keep their shape so we can build houses, make tools, furniture, clothes and shoes.
short.working: 1 mark for each correct use.

short.q: Describe two properties of a liquid.
short.answer: A liquid has a fixed volume and no shape of its own. It takes the shape of its container and can be poured.
short.working: 1 mark for each of two properties and 1 mark for the example.

short.q: Explain why a football is described as a container of matter although it looks empty.
short.answer: It is full of air. Air is a gas, so it has mass and takes up space. It keeps the ball in shape.
short.working: 1 mark for air inside, 1 mark for air being matter, 1 mark for it filling the ball.

short.q: Describe how you can show that a liquid takes the shape of its container.
short.answer: Pour 200 ml of water into a tall glass and then into a wide bowl. The shape of the water changes but the amount stays the same.
short.working: 1 mark for the two containers, 1 mark for shape changing, 1 mark for the volume the same.

short.q: A shopkeeper has 2 kg of sugar and 750 g of salt. Find the total mass in grams.
short.working: 1 mark for 2 kg = 2000 g, 1 mark for adding 750 g and 1 mark for the answer.

short.q: A jug has 1 litre of juice. 350 ml is poured into a cup. How much is left in the jug?
short.working: 1 mark for 1 litre = 1000 ml, 1 mark for the subtraction 1000 - 350 and 1 mark for the answer.

short.q: Name three gases and say how each is useful.
short.answer: Air or oxygen for breathing, cooking gas for cooking, air in tyres or footballs.
short.working: 1 mark for each gas with its use.

short.q: Explain why sand is not a liquid although it can be poured.
short.answer: Each grain of sand is a small solid with its own shape. The grains are piled together and pour as a pile.
short.working: 1 mark for grains being solids, 1 mark for grains having shape, 1 mark for conclusion.

short.q: Describe how you would show that air takes up space using a cup, tissue paper and a basin of water.
short.answer: Push dry tissue into the bottom of the cup. Turn the cup upside down and push it straight down into water. Lift it out. The tissue is dry because air took up the space in the cup and kept the water out.
short.working: 1 mark for set up, 1 mark for pushing into water, 1 mark for dry tissue, 1 mark for conclusion.

short.q: Compare solids, liquids and gases in terms of shape and volume.
short.answer: Solid: own shape and fixed volume. Liquid: takes shape of container, fixed volume. Gas: no shape and no fixed volume, fills the container.
short.working: 1 mark for each state with correct shape and volume, plus 1 mark for a comparison.

short.q: Write two uses of each of these: solids, liquids and gases. (Choose any four uses in all.)
short.answer: Solids: building, tools, clothes. Liquids: drinking, washing, cooking, fuel. Gases: breathing, cooking gas, inflating tyres.
short.working: 1 mark for each correct use up to 4.

short.q: Group these into solid, liquid and gas: milk, chalk, oxygen, cooking oil, book, steam.
short.answer: Solids: chalk and book. Liquids: milk and cooking oil. Gases: oxygen and steam.
short.working: 1 mark for each correct pair.

short.q: A jug holds 500 ml of water. Musa pours in 250 ml and later takes out 100 ml. How much water is in the jug at the end?
short.working: 1 mark for 500 + 250 = 750, 1 mark for 750 - 100, 1 mark for 650, 1 mark for the unit ml.

short.q: Explain why a kilogram of stones and a kilogram of feathers have the same mass but not the same volume.
short.answer: Both have 1 kg of matter. The feathers take up more space than the stones so their volume is larger.
short.working: 1 mark for equal mass, 1 mark for the meaning of mass, 1 mark for feathers taking more space, 1 mark for volume being space.

short.q: Describe an experiment to show that a solid keeps its shape but a liquid takes the shape of its container. State what you would observe.
short.answer: Use a stone and water. Put the stone in a cup and then in a bowl. It keeps its shape. Pour water in the cup and then into the bowl and its shape changes with the container. Conclusion: solids keep shape but liquids take the container's shape.
short.working: 1 mark for materials, 1 mark for stone in both containers, 1 mark for water in both, 1 mark for observation, 1 mark for conclusion.

short.q: Explain why steam from a kettle is invisible although we see a white cloud above the spout. Say what state of matter the cloud is.
short.answer: Steam is water as a gas and it is invisible. The white cloud is made of tiny water drops which are liquid.
short.working: 1 mark for steam is a gas, 1 mark for invisible, 1 mark for white cloud being tiny drops, 1 mark for liquid, 1 mark for a clear explanation.

short.q: Describe how you would measure 300 ml of water using a measuring jug, and how you would measure the mass of a mango.
short.answer: Place the jug on a flat surface, pour water until the level reaches the 300 mark with your eye level with the water. For the mango, place it on a balance and read the mass in grams.
short.working: 1 mark each for flat surface, pouring to 300 ml, eye level, using a balance, reading in grams.

short.q: A pupil says that empty containers have nothing inside. Explain why the pupil is wrong and how you would show it.
short.answer: They are full of air which is matter. Air takes up space. For example the upside-down cup pushed into water stays dry inside or a balloon swells with air.
short.working: 1 mark for air inside, 1 mark for air is matter, 1 mark for an activity, 1 mark for the observation, 1 mark for the conclusion.

short.q: Give two examples of decomposable waste and two of non-decomposable waste.
short.answer: Decomposable: vegetable peelings, dung, leaves. Non-decomposable: plastic, tin, glass.
short.working: 1 mark for each correct pair.

short.q: Name the three Rs of waste management.
short.answer: Reduce, reuse and recycle.
short.working: 1 mark for two and 2 marks for all three.

short.q: State two dangers of leaving waste in the environment.
short.answer: Blocked drains and floods, disease from flies and rats, harm to animals, injuries from glass.
short.working: 1 mark for each danger.

short.q: Why should you wear gloves when collecting waste?
short.answer: To protect your hands from cuts and germs.
short.working: 1 mark for cuts and 1 mark for germs.

short.q: Give two ways of reducing waste at home.
short.answer: Buy less packaging, carry a reusable bag, cook only what is needed, repair things.
short.working: 1 mark for each.

short.q: Explain the difference between reusing and recycling.
short.answer: Reusing means using an item again in the same or a new way without changing it, for example a bottle for water. Recycling means turning waste into a new product, for example melting old plastic.
short.working: 1 mark for reuse, 1 mark for recycle, 1 mark for one example.

short.q: Describe how kitchen waste can be turned into manure.
short.answer: Put peelings and other kitchen waste with dry leaves and some soil in a compost pit. Decomposers rot it and after some weeks it turns to compost.
short.working: 1 mark for the pit, 1 mark for decomposers, 1 mark for compost.

short.q: Describe how waste attracts pests that harm health.
short.answer: Rotting waste attracts flies, rats and cockroaches. They spread germs to food and cause diseases such as diarrhoea and cholera.
short.working: 1 mark for pests, 1 mark for germs, 1 mark for diseases.

short.q: Give three safety measures during waste management.
short.answer: Wear gloves and closed shoes, use a rake or shovel, do not touch sharp objects, wash hands afterwards, do not burn waste.
short.working: 1 mark for each.

short.q: Write three ways of managing waste in the classroom.
short.answer: Use a bin with a lid, put paper in a separate box for reusing, do not litter, make monitors.
short.working: 1 mark for each.

short.q: Explain why plastic bags are a danger to the environment.
short.answer: They stay for many years, block drains, harm animals that eat them and pollute land and water.
short.working: 1 mark for each of three points.

short.q: Describe how solid waste causes flooding in towns.
short.answer: Polythene bags and plastic block drains. Water cannot flow away when it rains. It gathers in the streets and floods homes and roads.
short.working: 1 mark for each point up to 4.

short.q: Sort into decomposable and non-decomposable: egg shells, tin can, cotton cloth, polythene bag, cow dung, glass bottle.
short.answer: Decomposable: egg shells, cotton cloth, cow dung. Non-decomposable: tin can, polythene bag, glass bottle.
short.working: Award 4 marks for all correct, 3 for five, 2 for four and 1 for three.

short.q: Describe how you would make a dustbin from locally available materials.
short.answer: Choose a strong bucket, box or container. Cut and smooth the top and cover any sharp edge. Make a lid if possible. Paint a label saying waste only and put it in a suitable place.
short.working: 1 mark for each of four steps.

short.q: Explain how a school can manage waste at the kitchen, classrooms and playground.
short.answer: Kitchen: compost pit for food waste and separate bin for plastic. Classroom: bin with lid and paper box. Playground: bins and monitors who pick litter.
short.working: 1 mark for each place and 1 mark for a clear system.

short.q: Explain why sorting waste is important for reusing and recycling.
short.answer: Sorting separates plastics, metals, glass, paper and food waste so each can be recycled, reused or composted without contaminating the others.
short.working: 1 mark for sorting, 1 mark for recycling, 1 mark for composting, 1 mark for clear link.

short.q: Suggest two ways to make toys or ornaments from waste and the materials needed.
short.answer: A toy car from a box and bottle tops. Beads from rolled paper. A flower vase from a tin.
short.working: 1 mark for each toy and 1 mark for each list of materials.

short.q: Explain the dangers of solid waste to health, animals and the environment.
short.answer: Health: flies and rats spread diseases, mosquitoes breed in tins. Animals: goats eat polythene and die. Environment: blocked drains, polluted water, harmful smoke from burning.
short.working: 2 marks for health, 1 mark for animals and 2 marks for environment.

short.q: Describe how you would organise the cleaning of a school compound using safe methods.
short.answer: Form groups with roles. Wear gloves and shoes. Use rakes and shovels. Sort waste into decomposable and non-decomposable bins. Take compost to the pit. Wash hands after.
short.working: 1 mark for each step up to 5.

short.q: Discuss how the three Rs can be used for waste from a school kitchen.
short.answer: Reduce: cook and serve only what is needed. Reuse: use empty oil tins for storage and sacks for carrying. Recycle: sell scrap metal and paper, compost peelings.
short.working: 1 mark for each R, 1 mark for one clear example and 1 mark for the compost point.

short.q: Explain why burning waste is not a good way of managing waste and give better methods.
short.answer: Burning gives harmful smoke, especially from plastic. Better: reduce, reuse, recycle, compost and use bins.
short.working: 2 marks for reasons and 3 marks for better methods.
